simple.meaning: נִפְקָא (niphqâʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an outgo , i.e. expense.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 6:4. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נִפְקָא (H5313) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נִפְקָא (niphqâʼ) / H5313 is traced through Ezra 6:4, Ezra 6:8 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

timeline.evidenceText: with three courses of great stones and a course of new timber. Let the expenses be given out of the king’s house.

Moreover I make a decree what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the building of this house of God: that of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the River, expenses must be given with all diligence to these men, that they not be hindered.
